solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Car's purpose — at root to do with self, in the first place

indicators.note: says the self piece is placed at the front, ahead of the word for purpose

parts.words: at root to do with self
parts.note: auto- is the Greek root meaning self, as in autobiography
a motive is the purpose behind an action

explanation.surface: A musing on what a car is for, and how its name comes from a root meaning self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car's' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition, an adjective meaning to do with cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Automotive describes anything relating to motor vehicles, so it stands for the possessive sense of car.

clue.text: 'Thank Heaven!' (clutches cross)

indicators.note: the exclamation grips the letters of the answer within its two words

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims thanks to heaven while gripping a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' holds the answer inside tHANK Heaven, across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankh is the ancient Egyptian looped cross, a symbol of life.

clue.text: After time, one fitting out ship set off

indicators.note: the rigging worker comes after the time letter, so it stands second

parts.note: a rigger fits a ship with its ropes and sails

explanation.surface: After a while, a shipwright sets something off.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, as a trigger fires a gun.

clue.text: Bring two sides together? To do so will result in happiness for Micawber

definitions.meaning: playfully, to make the two ends of something meet, closing a gap

definitions.text: To do so will result in happiness for Micawber
definitions.meaning: Mr Micawber in Dickens's David Copperfield says spending just within income means happiness, i.e. living within one's means

explanation.surface: The setter, who calls himself Micawber, borrows his namesake's famous recipe for happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Micawber in David Copperfield: income twenty pounds, spending nineteen pounds nineteen and six, result happiness. The setter uses the same pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To make ends meet is the idiom for earning just enough to cover one's spending.

clue.text: Red European's top supporter

parts.note: tent is a dark red Spanish wine, once used as communion wine
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A left-wing continental is the leading backer of some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' suggests a communist, but here it is TENT, an old name for a deep red Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent pole holds up the top of a tent, so it literally supports the top.

clue.text: Empty container inside another

indicators.note: says one vessel sits within the other one

parts.note: a vat is another kind of container, following on from the first
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Nested empty vessels, one inside the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied or holding nothing, a synonym of empty.

clue.text: Do Burberrys over?

indicators.note: turned over, so the raincoats' word is read from the end back

parts.note: Burberry is a British brand of raincoat, so Burberrys are macs (mackintoshes)

explanation.surface: A question about redoing some designer raincoats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the start of a question but is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, and a scam is a swindle.

clue.text: Underground worker runs after dog

indicators.note: the runs letter comes after the dog, at the end

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A miner hurries along behind a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, who works below ground.

clue.text: Troubled teen — minor's in the soup

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters of the youngsters' words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A troubled teenager, a minor, is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' reads as the idiom for being in trouble, but only 'soup' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: It takes skill to go after king and steal ornament

indicators.note: the skill word is placed after the king and steal pieces

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to nick is British slang for to steal
a knack is a skill

explanation.surface: A burglar needs skill to steal from a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A knick-knack is a small decorative trinket, a little ornament.

clue.text: Type of oven that'll take large pastry dish

indicators.note: the oven word will take in, holding the large letter inside it

parts.note: a fan oven circulates hot air
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A kitchen choosing an oven big enough for a tart.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, a pastry dish.

clue.text: You can watch this part of blood test

parts.note: plasma is the liquid part of blood
to screen is to test, as in medical screening

explanation.surface: A medical blood test you can observe.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasma screen is a flat-panel television display, something one watches.

clue.text: After setback, I'll bandage left eye up

indicators.note: will wrap around, so the self word encloses the left letter
set back means the self word is read backwards

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: Someone after an injury promises to bandage their left eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye up' looks like part of the injury but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone lecherously, which is to eye them up.

clue.text: Draws must follow panel's arrangement for how they can be settled

indicators.note: the draws word comes after the rearranged group word
rearranging the letters of the group word puts them in a new order

parts.note: the group word, with its possessive ending as a link
draws in a match are ties

explanation.surface: A panel decides how drawn matches are to be resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's on 'panel's' is only a link; 'arrangement' works on the five letters of the bare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn football ties are often settled by a penalty shootout, so penalties are how draws are decided.

clue.text: Light structure precariously balanced on middle of decoration

indicators.note: in a down answer, the scrambled part sits on top of the central letters
shakily placed, so the letters of the steady word are jumbled
takes the centre letters of the ornament word

explanation.surface: Something light perched shakily on top of a centrepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precariously' rearranges BALANCED to CANDELAB, and 'middle of' gives RA from decoRAtion.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched holder for several candles, a structure carrying lights.

clue.text: Broadcast: 'Beer is man's best friend'

parts.note: a programme that was broadcast was aired
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A TV announcement claims beer is man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An Airedale is a breed of terrier, and a dog is proverbially man's best friend.

clue.text: You say you are certain inside, his rates are extortionate?

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
spoken aloud, the two words sound like the two letters U and R

parts.note: said aloud, these words are the letters U R
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone insisting, deep down, that a moneylender charges too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places SURE within U R, the letters that sound like 'you are'.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at exorbitant interest, so his rates are extortionate.

clue.text: Identify mistake in dosage

indicators.note: an error in the letters, so they are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A doctor or pharmacist spots an error in a dose.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify an illness or problem from its symptoms.

clue.text: Party winning masses over has source of power

indicators.note: the party word wins, taking possession of the other letters inside

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for masses is read backwards

parts.note: masses means many

explanation.surface: A political party wins over the masses and gains power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party winning masses over' reads as an election victory, but 'over' is a reversal and 'winning' a containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator producing electric current, a source of power.

clue.text: Like cake that's plain, perhaps, or spotted

definitions.meaning: split as ..., describing a plain cake without icing

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as NOT ICED, a plain cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted, in the sense of seen, is a synonym for noticed.

clue.text: Free on bail — it means celebratory drink

indicators.note: set free, so the letters of the three words are loosed into a new order

explanation.surface: Released on bail, someone celebrates with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink poured as an offering, or jokingly any celebratory drink.

clue.text: Sound of charger perhaps seizing victory after I launch attack

indicators.note: the horse sound with its captured letter comes after the I
the horse sound seizes the victory letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a charger is a warhorse, and a horse neighs

explanation.surface: A cavalry charge, the warhorse whinnying as it takes victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charger' looks like a battery charger but is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigh is to speak out violently against something, launching a verbal attack.

clue.text: Get on a bit, doddery

indicators.note: shaky and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone getting on a bit and becoming doddery.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, a synonym of get.

clue.text: Group of youngsters pester antisocial character

parts.note: a litter is a group of young animals born together
to bug someone is to pester them

explanation.surface: A gang of kids harassing someone unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug drops rubbish in public places, an antisocial person.

clue.text: Fellow that's used by smugglers?

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a man or chap
a small sheltered bay, traditionally where smugglers landed contraband

explanation.definitionFit: Cove means both an old slang word for a chap and a small coastal inlet used for landing goods.

clue.text: Break is critical on northward journey

indicators.note: in a down answer, travelling north means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: pans means criticises harshly, is critical of

explanation.surface: A breakdown during a trip north is a critical matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly, and a snap is a break.

clue.text: Does mate with one resist?

definitions.meaning: the male deer that mates with does
to ... a trend is to resist it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb but is plural of doe, a female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is the male of deer, partner to does, and to buck means to oppose.

clue.text: Royal family's survival after removal of head of government by Scotsman

indicators.note: the leading letter of the ruling word is taken out of the survival word

parts.note: a hangover is something surviving from an earlier time

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty survives a change of government thanks to a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removal of head of government' takes G from HANGOVER to leave HANOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoverian describes the House of Hanover, the British royal dynasty from George I to Victoria.

clue.text: Slash is central to this band that's current (kind of)

definitions.text: Slash is central to this band
definitions.meaning: the rock band ... has a slash in the middle of its name
... means alternating or direct current, an electrical term

explanation.walkthrough: Slash is also a famous guitarist, though not in this band.
explanation.definitionFit: AC/DC names both the Australian hard rock group and the alternating or direct electric supply.

clue.text: Put in prison hulk for training

parts.note: to intern is to confine or imprison, especially in wartime
a hulk is an old ship, once used as a floating prison

explanation.surface: A convict is locked up on a prison hulk.
explanation.walkthrough: Prison hulks were decommissioned ships used as jails in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An internship is a period of work experience, a form of training.
